title: DiscoveredKB
description: One knowledge base the Semiont launcher manages on this machine, as published in the discovery document (see DiscoveryDocument). Endpoints and identity only — never credentials; login remains the consumer's per-KB business.

host.description: Hostname the KB is reachable on from this machine (today always "localhost" — local stacks bind locally and codespace KBs arrive through a local port forward)

port.description: Local TCP port of the KB's API (the backend port for a local stack; the allocated forward port for a codespace stack)

placement.description: Where the stack actually runs. "local": containers on this machine. "codespace": a GitHub-hosted VM whose KB is port-forwarded here.

repo.description: owner/name GitHub slug — present for codespace placements, where the repo is the stack's identity

did.description: The KB's did:web identifier, from its committed .semiont/config — "did:web:" + the [site] domain, verbatim. REQUIRED: a KB that declares no domain has no identity to publish, and the launcher refuses to start it rather than inventing or defaulting one. NOT unique within a document: a did names the knowledge base, not a running copy of it, so a local clone and a codespace of the same repo legitimately share one and both are published. host:port is the unique field (at most one entry per address), so consumers look up by ADDRESS and use the did to VERIFY that the copy they reached is the KB they meant — an address alone cannot say which KB is which, and an identity alone cannot say which copy.

siteName.description: Human-readable site name from the KB's .semiont/config, for display

managedBy.description: The agent that owns this entry's lifecycle (the launcher writes "semiont-launcher"). Consumers treat managed entries as authoritative for themselves — upsert on appearance, remove on disappearance — and never touch entries they did not write.
